metadata.formula: For F ≥ 0, integrate the superlevel measures over the positive level variable. Gaussian: E[(R−L)₊] = ∫₀∞ P(R>L+s) ds. Kernel: ∫ f d(μ−ν) = ∫₀¹ (μ{f≥s}−ν{f≥s}) ds for f=K(·,t)∈[0,1]. Doob: ∫⁻ (f*)^p = p ∫₀∞ μ{f*≥s} s^(p−1) ds in the nonnegative extended sense.
metadata.mechanism: Convert a nonnegative observable, or the difference of its integrals under two laws, to level-set measures and integrate the available estimate. Gaussian uses exponential Markov and the positive-part boundary term. Kernel uses the same bounded observable and the unit length of the level interval. Doob uses a weighted level integral, a weak-type maximal estimate, Fubini, Hölder and upper truncation.

hypothesis_map.gaussian: Actual standard Gaussian row, r=q+1, 2q+1<d, literal L≥0. Finite radius moment and an integrable exponential envelope support ordinary real integrals.
hypothesis_map.kernel: Probability μ and ν, a common measurable Markov kernel, measurable output event t, and uniform event discrepancy ≤δ. Its event probability lies in [0,1].
hypothesis_map.doob: Nonnegative discrete-time submartingale on a finite measure space, fixed finite horizon n and p>1. The weighted layer identity alone uses nonnegative measurable f* and p>0.

conclusion_map.gaussian: The tail envelope integrates to 3/(1000d) and the boundary term contributes L/(1000d), giving the strict truncated first-moment bound.
conclusion_map.kernel: The integral of a pointwise absolute discrepancy bounded by δ on the unit level interval gives factor-one eventwise contraction.
conclusion_map.doob: The weak-type estimate and Hölder yield the strong eLpNorm comparison with factor p/(p−1), including the extended-valued interpretation.

metadata.failure_boundary: The Gaussian numerical bound uses the fixed standard-law exponential moment and the finite positive threshold scale. Eventwise TV alone gives no bound on an unbounded observable or unbounded cost. Kernel contraction here uses a common kernel and the unit interval. The Doob p/(p−1) route requires p>1 and the submartingale estimate. The different truncations and probability laws supply no theorem implication between these applications.
metadata.canonical_API_rule: Use the actual named Mathlib Layercake APIs as shared canonical declarations where they occur. The three specialized applications have separate types and proofs.

scope: Conceptual comparison proposed for independent validation and later serialized graph integration.
